---
argmap-version: 0.2
title: "Concept: one half, and what a conditional does not touch"
description: "A conditional says nothing about its own premise. Three blocks, identical but for one line, so the reading sits side by side on one plane. Block 1 is the bare conditional: the unauthored premise reads one half, where the map leaves a claim nothing speaks to, and the conclusion reads 0.70. Block 2 pins the premise at one half and nothing changes. Block 3 states the converse the source also asserts, and the conclusion returns to one half while the premise stays put. Until 2026-09-08 this file taught the opposite lesson, the drift tax of the retired uniform reference (its antecedent pull, SOLVER_SEMANTICS P8): under that solve block 1 read the premise at 1/(1+2^0.8) = 0.3648. The network reference D161 ships has no such pull, and the file was re-read for it."
---

# ===========================================================================
# READ THIS FIRST (re-read 2026-09-08 under D161, the G network reference).
# A conditional touches its CONCLUSION and leaves its PREMISE alone.
#
# The node to watch in each block below is @rain, the antecedent, which
# nobody authored a number for: it reads one half in every block, because one
# half is where the map leaves a claim nothing speaks to. @fire, the
# consequent, is what the line moves: 0.8 of the premise's worlds fire the
# rule and the rest are filled evenly, so 0.5 * (0.8 + 0.2 * 0.5) + 0.5 * 0.5
# = 0.70. Block 3's converse line fills the not-rain worlds too, and the
# conclusion returns to one half.
#
# UNTIL 2026-09-08 THIS FILE TAUGHT THE DRIFT TAX: under the retired uniform
# reference (solve_map.py --reference d36) a bare conditional pulled its
# unauthored premise down to 1/(1+2^0.8) = 0.3648 (MATH.md's old worked
# example), block 2's pin cancelled it and block 3's converse cancelled it
# from the other side. D161 item 1 retired that solve and its pull
# (SOLVER_SEMANTICS P8 closed); the per-block numbers below carry both
# readings, dated. The strengths stay 0.8 throughout so the arithmetic is
# the only thing on screen. Nothing here is a claim about rain or fires.
#
# RESIDUAL DISCIPLINE (D36 rule 3), which this tier keeps and the older
# examples/ files do not: pins live only on frontier roots. @rain2 carries
# one because it is a root and block 2's whole point is that it does.
# @fire, @fire2 and @fire3 are concluded into and therefore carry no pin;
# a `# check:` would be the place for an author's own audit number, and
# these three deliberately assert none, because the conclusion is not what
# the file is about.
# ===========================================================================

# ---- block 1: the bare conditional. @rain is never authored. ---------------
# Solved 2026-09-08 (the default reference G, solve_map.py): @rain 0.500,
# @fire 0.700. Under the retired reference (--reference d36; 2026-08-04):
# @rain 0.365, @fire 0.643, where 0.365 is 1/(1+2^0.8) to three places.

@rain [It rained last night]: no number, on purpose; it reads one half  # tour: drift-tax
@fire [The fire was put out]:
$douse [rain that heavy puts out a fire that size] 0.8 @fire | @rain: the whole block is this one assertion, and it says nothing at all about how likely rain was  # tour: drift-tax

# ---- block 2: the same conditional, antecedent authored ------------------
# Solved 2026-09-08 (G): @rain2 0.500, @fire2 0.700, identical to block 1:
# a pin at one half asserts what the map already read. Under d36
# (2026-08-04): @rain2 0.499, @fire2 0.697, the pin cancelling the pull
# (MATH.md's old Adams restoration).

@rain2 [It rained last night] 0.5: a frontier root, so a pin belongs here  # tour: drift-tax
@fire2 [The fire was put out]:
$douse2 [rain that heavy puts out a fire that size] 0.8 @fire2 | @rain2: the identical step; the only difference in this block is the number on the line above

# ---- block 3: the converse asserted as well ------------------------------
# The $no-doom-otherwise shape from the flagship map: a source that asserts
# "if it rained, the fire went out" often also asserts "and otherwise it did
# not", and writing the second one down is ordinary authoring, not a trick.
# Solved 2026-09-08 (G): @rain3 0.500, @fire3 0.500: the converse fills the
# not-rain worlds, so the CONCLUSION moves (0.700 to 0.500) and the premise
# does not. Under d36 (2026-08-04) the same pair read 0.500 / 0.500, there
# because two equal and opposite pulls cancelled exactly.

@rain3 [It rained last night]: still no number, and still one half  # tour: drift-tax
@fire3 [The fire was put out]:
$douse3 [rain that heavy puts out a fire that size] 0.8 @fire3 | @rain3:
$nodouse3 [a fire that size does not go out on its own] 0.8 ~@fire3 | ~@rain3: the converse, stated where a reader can argue with it instead of hiding in a prior  # tour: drift-tax

# ---- why this matters when you are authoring for real ---------------------
# Under the shipped solve a map may assert as many conditionals as its source
# does without dragging their premises anywhere: an unauthored premise reads
# one half until a line concludes into it or its author writes a number.
# What a conditional leaves open is the OTHER half of its own case, the
# worlds where the premise fails, and the map fills those evenly. So the
# converse is still worth writing where the source asserts it ($nodouse3,
# the flagship's $no-doom-otherwise): it is content about the conclusion,
# and it moves the conclusion. The drift tax this file used to demonstrate
# is recorded above as the retired reference's limit (D161 item 1).
